memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Diagnosis: Major depressive disorder, moderate episode; and Type 2 diabetes mellitus, newly diagnosed.
Evidence: PHQ-9 score 14, random plasma glucose 186 mg/dL, HbA1c 7.8% (to be confirmed). Patient reports low mood, anhedonia, fatigue for 8 weeks, plus polyuria, nocturia, and mild weight gain. Examination: BMI 27.4 kg/m2, BP 128/82 mmHg, lungs clear, no focal neurology.
Inhaler technique: not applicable (no inhaler prescribed). Smoking status: never smoker; pack-years 0. Spirometry: FEV1 2.8 L (92% predicted), FVC 3.2 L, FEV1/FVC 0.88.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Sertraline 50 mg OD
Metformin 500 mg BD
Glimepiride 1 mg OD before breakfast
Sitagliptin 100 mg OD
Empagliflozin 10 mg OD

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Dilated fundus exam: No microaneurysms, no hemorrhages, macula intact. Mild peripheral retinal vascular tortuosity. No signs of diabetic retinopathy.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: Feeling a bit better mood‑wise, but metformin is causing loose stools and mild nausea most mornings. Otherwise energy is up and thirst less.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Diagnosis: Major depressive disorder, improving; Type 2 diabetes mellitus, suboptimal control.
Evidence: PHQ-9 now 9, HbA1c 7.6%, fasting glucose 132 mg/dL, metformin GI intolerance.
Patient reports improved mood but persistent loose stools with metformin; weight stable; BP 126/80.
Inhaler technique: not applicable. Smoking status: never smoker; pack-years 0. Spirometry: FEV1 2.9 L (95% predicted), FVC 3.3 L, FEV1/FVC 0.88; change in FEV1 +0.1 L since last test.
